cards.text: The prophet Isaiah is carrying a message from the LORD to His people, Israel. The LORD calls Himself their Redeemer, the One who formed them from the womb. Then He starts reading off His résumé, and friend, it is LONG.

cards.question: First on the list: the LORD made all things. True or false: the LORD says He had help stretching out the heavens.

cards.text: Next, He foils the signs of false prophets and makes fools of diviners. Their predictions fall apart like a weather app promising sunshine while you're standing in a downpour.

cards.question: The LORD confounds the wise and turns their knowledge into ___.

cards.text: When His servant brings a message, the LORD confirms it. Then He says of Jerusalem, “She will be inhabited,” and He has a word for the ruined cities of Judah too.

cards.question: The LORD says the ruined cities of Judah will be ___.

cards.text: And the résumé keeps going. The LORD even has something to say to the depths of the sea.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell the depths of the sea?

cards.text: Heavens, earth, the sea, and then out of NOWHERE there's a name on the list: Cyrus, king of Persia (Ezra 1:1). I'd have read that line twice.

cards.question: The LORD says Cyrus will fulfill all that He desires. What does the LORD call Cyrus?
Along with Jerusalem being rebuilt, the LORD says the temple's foundation will be laid.

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks straight to Cyrus and calls him His anointed. He says He has grasped Cyrus's right hand.

cards.question: The LORD has grasped Cyrus's right hand. What for?

answers.text: To bless the work of his hands
To lead him into the temple

cards.text: Kings get disarmed before Cyrus, and doors open so the gates won't be shut. But there's still a lot in the way: mountains, gates of bronze, bars of iron.

cards.question: Mountains, gates of bronze and bars of iron stand in Cyrus's way. Who goes ahead of him to deal with them?

cards.text: The LORD goes before Cyrus, levels the mountains and breaks down the gates of bronze. Friend, one flimsy wooden drawer kept me in the dark for YEARS, and He breaks down BRONZE.
Then the LORD promises Cyrus the treasures of darkness and riches hidden in secret places. The best hidden treasure in my old junk drawer was a coupon that expired years ago.

cards.question: The LORD gives Cyrus these hidden riches so that Cyrus may ___ that He is the LORD, the God of Israel.

cards.text: Back to Cyrus. Now the LORD tells him why He's calling him by name.

cards.question: The LORD calls Cyrus by name for the sake of ___ His servant.
Cyrus already knew the LORD when the LORD gave him a title of honor.

cards.text: Cyrus gets a title of honor from the LORD, though Cyrus has not known Him. That's like getting promoted by a boss you've never met, and you don't even know what FLOOR they work on.
Then the LORD says it plain: “I am the LORD, and there is no other; there is no God but Me.” And He'll equip Cyrus for battle, though Cyrus has not known Him.

cards.question: The LORD equips Cyrus for battle. What's the bigger reason?

answers.text: So all may know there is none but Him
So Cyrus will rule the whole earth
So Persia will be feared forever

cards.text: Next, the LORD says He forms the light and creates the darkness.

cards.question: The LORD forms light and creates darkness. What else does He say He brings and creates?

cards.text: “I, the LORD, do all these things.” Then He calls the heavens to drip down from above and the skies to pour down righteousness.

cards.question: The LORD calls the earth to open up so that ___ may sprout, with righteousness springing up alongside it.

cards.text: Then comes a warning. Woe to the one who quarrels with his Maker.

cards.question: In the LORD's warning, the one who quarrels with his Maker is pictured as what?

cards.text: “Does the clay ask the potter, ‘What are you making?’” Picture cookie dough looking up mid-press asking ME that, when friend, I AM the stamp.

cards.question: The LORD gives a second warning: woe to the one who asks his father and mother what they have brought forth.

cards.text: Then the LORD, the Holy One of Israel and its Maker, speaks. He asks whether anyone will question Him about His sons, or instruct Him in the work of His hands.

cards.question: The LORD says He made the earth, but someone else stretched out the heavens.

cards.text: Then the LORD comes back to Cyrus. He'll raise him up in righteousness and make all his ways straight, and Cyrus will rebuild His city and set His exiles free.

cards.question: Cyrus will rebuild the LORD's city and set His exiles free. What does the LORD say about Cyrus being paid?

answers.text: It isn't for payment or reward
It's for a share of the temple gold
It's for the land of Judah

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess the exact words the LORD says to the sea. Card 7 gives nothing to reason from, and 'Be calm' is just as believable as 'Be dry', so the pick comes down to luck.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the exact name in 'for the sake of Jacob My servant'. Nothing before it links Jacob to Israel, and David and Moses are both believable as 'His servant'. The baker can only guess, not reason it out. Card 1 needs to give context, or the question needs to change.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: 'Back to Cyrus' suggests the passage stepped away from Cyrus, but 45:3 runs straight into 45:4 with the LORD still talking to him. The card also refers to 'why He's calling him by name', but no card ever told the baker that the LORD calls Cyrus by name (end of 45:3).

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This story card repeats the answer card 3 just revealed (a title of honor, though Cyrus has not known Him) and adds no new piece of the passage. Only the joke is new.
The right answer 'salvation' is abstract, while 'wheat' and 'cedars' are literal plants. The answers aren't the same kind of thing, so the right one stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The statement says the person asks 'his father and mother what they have brought forth'. The text gives two separate questions joined by 'or': to his father, 'What have you begotten?', and to his mother, 'What have you brought forth?'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This card asks again whether someone else stretched out the heavens, which stop 1 card 2 already asked (44:24). Meanwhile 45:12's new details, that He created man upon the earth and ordained all their host, are never told.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: The joke ends 'I AM the stamp', with 'I AM' in capitals, right after the potter-and-clay line about the LORD. It echoes God's name ('I AM WHO I AM', Exodus 3:14) and puts Papa Dorin in the Maker's role.
findings.question: Is capitalizing 'I AM' acceptable for Papa Dorin, and can he cast himself as the potter in this comparison, or does the reverence section rule this out?
